phase_title: Phase 4: gstack Sync and AAW Packaging Repair

findings.description: The upstream test/build suite does not pass on this machine (bun run test:windows -> exit=1, 7 failing tests). Every failure was re-run in isolation and attributed: 3 need jq on PATH, 2 need Windows Developer Mode (symlink privilege), 1 is a Git Bash fork() flake, 1 is a genuine upstream defect at browse/test/build.test.ts:16 predating the sync. This criterion was explicitly WAIVED at the phase-4 gate on 2026-08-26 by human decision (recorded inline in .advanced-plans/phases/phase-4/plan.md:61-78). Per the invoking instructions this is recorded as a failed criterion honestly, and per the waiver it does not by itself drive the overall verdict to fail.

Two rows in the Key Deliverables table name evidence filenames that do not match the files actually produced. 'gstack sync evidence' is listed as `.advanced-plans/evidence/<date>-gstack-sync.md` but the file actually produced is `.advanced-plans/evidence/2026-08-26-phase-4-loop-001-gstack-sync.md` (plus a second file `2026-08-26-fork-divergence-reaudit.md` covering todos 1-2). 'Idempotency evidence' is listed as `.advanced-plans/evidence/<date>-packaging-repair.md` but the idempotency proof (loop-003-4, ACC-16, uninstall preservation) is entirely inside `.advanced-plans/evidence/2026-08-26-phase-4-loop-003-installation-state.md`; the file actually named `2026-08-26-phase-4-loop-002-packaging-repair.md` contains zero occurrences of the word 'idempot'. This is the same discrepancy noted in the attempt-1 review and it still stands. The underlying evidence exists and was verified; only the deliverable table's filename claim is wrong.
findings.evidence: Glob of .advanced-plans/evidence/2026-08-26-phase-4-* returned loop-001-gstack-sync.md, loop-002-packaging-repair.md, loop-003-installation-state.md, none matching the plan's literal `<date>-gstack-sync.md` / `<date>-packaging-repair.md` patterns; Grep for 'idempot' (case-insensitive) in 2026-08-26-phase-4-loop-002-packaging-repair.md returned no matches, while 2026-08-26-phase-4-loop-003-installation-state.md:1-90 contains the idempotency-proof narrative

findings.description: Raw `~` remains in Step R2's fenced commands (`cp ... ~/.claude/skills/setup-with-claude/SKILL.md`, the curl -o target) and in prose. The file states this is deliberate: those commands are printed for the user to paste into their own external terminal ('Tell the user to run the command in a terminal outside this Claude Code session' — line 638), so the user's own shell resolves `~`, not this skill's own logic. This is judged sound: it is consistent with the file's own test ('who does the resolving: this skill, or the user' — line 728) and does not contradict the success criterion, which is about paths the installer itself resolves.

failure_notes: The gstack upstream suite criterion (bun run test:windows) fails honestly on this machine (exit=1, 7 failing tests) and is recorded as failed in criteria_outcomes; a human waiver dated 2026-08-26 covers only the passing half, not the recording half, and per the reviewing instructions does not by itself fail the gate. Open remediation items (install jq, enable Windows Developer Mode, report browse/test/build.test.ts:16 upstream) are tracked in .advanced-plans/PLANNING.md:25,36-37.

Two Key Deliverables table rows (gstack sync evidence, idempotency evidence) name evidence filenames that do not match the files actually produced; this is a documentation-table defect, not a missing-evidence defect, and does not affect any success criterion outcome.
summary: This is a re-review of phase 4 (attempt 2) after two changes stated in the invocation: a fix to two ~/HOME path resolutions in .claude/skills/setup-with-claude/SKILL.md (Step 6 global glue-skill copy, Step U7 global removal check), and a human waiver of the gstack-suite-passes half of one criterion. I independently inspected the fixed installer skill occurrence-by-occurrence: both Step 6 (line 269-270) and Step U7 (lines 532, 540-541) now resolve the global profile through <profile> (%USERPROFILE%) exactly as Step 1 mandates, matching the corresponding fix already verified clean in .aaw/detect.py. Every remaining raw '~' in the file is either prose stating the no-tilde rule, a description of POSIX/macOS user-shell behaviour, or the Step R2 fenced commands explicitly carved out because the user's own terminal (outside this Claude Code session) does the resolving, not the skill — a carve-out I judge sound because it tracks who performs the resolution, which is the substance of the criterion. The .aaw/installed.schema.json also enforces the no-~/no-%/no-$ rule at the schema level (line 58 regex). All five gstack criteria and all seven AAW-packaging criteria were checked against concrete artefacts: the sync branch head is byte-identical to upstream/main with a correct merge-base-diff re-verification and a local-only backup tag (loop-001 evidence), the Windows install smoke exits 0 with the live profile verified untouched, the branch carries only two untracked (uncommitted) test fixtures and no AAW-specific commits, the .gitignore whitelist now admits exactly one added directory (gstack-to-plans) alongside the existing setup-with-claude entry, the glue skill is present and its tracked status is corroborated by tests/packaging/test-fresh-clone.sh (which asserts git ls-files membership and was proven, in evidence, to PASS 13/13 on HEAD and FAIL when sources are removed or truncated), and tests/packaging/test-idempotency.sh implements a 43-check, nine-stage proof of ACC-16 (refresh-twice no-op), uninstall content-preservation, and reinstall convergence, entirely against a temporary project and a fake profile. The one criterion that does not pass on this machine — the upstream suite — is recorded as failed on its merits, exactly as the invoking instructions required, and is covered by an explicit, evidenced human waiver that the instructions say should not by itself fail the gate. Two Key Deliverables table rows name evidence files under a naming pattern that does not match what was actually produced (a documentation defect carried over from attempt 1, not a missing-evidence defect). No critical, high-confidence finding remains that would independently fail the gate, so the overall verdict is pass.
